prompt: What is NIC teaming used for on a vSphere standard switch?
options: Providing multiple uplink paths under a configured selection/failover policy
Replicating DNS zones between hosts
Joining every guest to Active Directory
Mounting every available storage export
en: Teaming combines eligible uplinks; its actual behavior depends on policy and upstream connectivity.
ru: Teaming eligible uplinks deta hai; actual behavior policy aur upstream connectivity par depend karta hai.

prompt: What does Active mean in a teaming policy?
options: Eligible to carry normal traffic under that policy
Reserved only for a failure event
Excluded from every traffic path
Guaranteed to carry half of every flow
en: Active eligibility does not guarantee equal traffic on each link.
ru: Active eligibility har link par equal traffic ki guarantee nahin.

prompt: What is a Standby adapter’s intended role?
options: A backup eligible when active uplink paths fail
A permanently forbidden adapter
A writable primary DNS server
A guarantee of twice the single-flow speed
en: Standby offers an alternate path when the active configuration cannot carry traffic.
ru: Standby active configuration fail honay par alternate path deta hai.

prompt: What does Unused mean for an adapter in a particular teaming policy?
options: It is excluded from that policy’s normal traffic and failover
It is permanently unusable in every enterprise
It is always the first backup adapter
It must have a missing hardware driver
en: Unused is a policy-specific exclusion, not a universal hardware verdict.
ru: Unused policy-specific exclusion hai, universal hardware verdict nahin.

prompt: Under originating virtual port ID, how is traffic normally assigned?
options: A virtual port uses a selected uplink rather than splitting every flow across all uplinks
Each packet is always divided equally across all links
The DNS suffix picks the fastest router
Every guest needs a manually configured IP hash
en: Originating-port selection does not promise multiplied bandwidth for one virtual port.
ru: Originating-port selection aik virtual port ki multiplied bandwidth promise nahin karti.

prompt: What does Link status only failure detection monitor?
options: The NIC’s reported link state
Every upstream router’s application health
The latest DNS zone serial
The current datastore’s free capacity
en: A link can remain up while a failure farther upstream prevents communication.
ru: Link up reh sakta hai jab upstream failure communication rok de.

prompt: What does Failback enabled allow after an eligible preferred link recovers?
options: Traffic can return to the recovered preferred path according to policy
Every VM is migrated to another ESXi host
A standby adapter is deleted automatically
All client DNS settings are restored
en: Failback concerns return to a recovered network path, not VM migration.
ru: Failback recovered network path par wapsi hai, VM migration nahin.

prompt: What is Notify switches intended to help update after a traffic-path change?
options: Upstream MAC forwarding information
Windows user password history
The DNS primary suffix
The VM’s disk partition layout
en: Network notifications help upstream switches relearn where relevant MAC traffic is reachable.
ru: Network notifications upstream switches ko relevant MAC traffic ka raasta relearn karne mein madad karti hain.

prompt: What does a port-group teaming override change?
options: That group’s effective teaming policy instead of inherited settings
Every switch on every ESXi host automatically
Only the computer’s DNS suffix
Only the guest disk controller
en: Inspect inheritance and overrides to know which policy a group actually uses.
ru: Group ki actual policy ke liye inheritance aur overrides inspect hon.

prompt: What is the purpose of explicit failover order?
options: Prioritizing eligible uplinks rather than application-aware load balancing
Moving busy VMs between hosts using DRS
Selecting links by DNS answer order
Dividing all traffic into fixed application categories
en: Explicit failover order is a network-path preference policy, not DRS.
ru: Explicit failover order network-path preference policy hai, DRS nahin.

prompt: Both vmnic0 and vmnic1 appear Active in a screenshot. Which statement is justified?
options: Both are eligible in that captured configuration; failover still needs testing
A single transfer has verified 20 Gbit/s throughput
Both links are proven physically independent
Every application session survived a real fault
en: Membership evidence is not performance or failure-recovery evidence.
ru: Membership evidence performance ya failure-recovery evidence nahin.

prompt: A student removes vmnic1 from the switch and calls it a complete failover test. What is the correction?
options: Administrative removal is not the same as testing recovery from a link fault
Any removal automatically proves all failure cases
A removed adapter remains the policy’s Standby
Removing the adapter verifies IP-hash consistency
en: A controlled failure test observes traffic on configured alternate paths during a fault.
ru: Controlled failure test fault ke dauran configured alternate paths par traffic observe karta hai.

prompt: A lab wants to test Active/Standby with the originating-port policy. Which arrangement fits?
options: One lab uplink Active and another compatible lab uplink Standby
Both lab uplinks Unused
Only one uplink, with all backups deleted
A DNS A record labelled Standby
en: The backup must be configured as an eligible alternate path.
ru: Backup eligible alternate path ke taur par configured hona chahiye.

prompt: Two lab uplinks are mapped to unrelated Workstation networks. What must be checked before treating them as equivalent failover paths?
options: Both reach the intended compatible Layer-2 network/VLAN and endpoint
Only that their adapter numbers are consecutive
Only that their link-speed labels match
Only that both port-group names are uppercase
en: Teaming does not make unrelated outer networks interchangeable.
ru: Teaming unrelated outer networks ko interchangeable nahin banati.

prompt: Which endpoint arrangement best tests that traffic actually uses an uplink?
options: An external peer whose path crosses the tested uplink
Two compatible VMs whose traffic stays inside the same host
A guest pinging its own loopback address
A browser reading a local text file
en: An external path is needed to exercise uplink failover rather than local switching.
ru: Local switching ke bajaye uplink failover exercise karne ke liye external path chahiye.

prompt: How should an outer Workstation NIC be identified before simulating a lab link fault?
options: Match its MAC address to the intended ESXi vmnic
Assume Network Adapter 5 always means vmnic4
Pick the first enabled Windows adapter
Disable every outer adapter and inspect afterward
en: MAC mapping helps avoid disconnecting management or an unrelated network.
ru: MAC mapping management ya unrelated network disconnect karne se bachati hai.

prompt: Both uplinks are Active under originating-port selection, but one transfer uses one uplink. What is the best interpretation?
options: This can be normal for one virtual port under that policy
Active/Active must always double every transfer
The second uplink must be physically broken
DNS must distribute the packets evenly
en: Observe multiple virtual ports and counters before judging distribution.
ru: Distribution judge karne se pehle multiple virtual ports aur counters observe karein.

prompt: The tested link is restored and Failback is enabled. What should the test record include?
options: Recovery after reconnection and the final saved/effective policy
Only the original pre-fault screenshot
Only a public DNS lookup
Only the guest’s wallpaper
en: A complete exercise records baseline, fault, recovery and restored state.
ru: Complete exercise baseline, fault, recovery aur restored state record karti hai.

prompt: Two nested NICs depend on one desktop physical NIC and Windows host. What does their failover test not prove?
options: Independent physical hardware redundancy
That a virtual link fault was simulated
That an alternate virtual path may work
That configured traffic recovered in the observed test
en: Shared outer hardware remains a common failure dependency.
ru: Shared outer hardware common failure dependency rehti hai.

prompt: A proposal uses 172.16.50.0/24 while existing STORAGE is 172.16.0.102/16. What must be resolved before the test?
options: The overlapping subnet plan and the actual intended routing/path
Only the spelling of the VM names
Only whether both uplinks report Full duplex
Nothing because different third octets prevent overlap
en: The proposed /24 lies inside the existing /16 and needs deliberate redesign or verified alternatives.
ru: Proposed /24 existing /16 ke andar hai; deliberate redesign ya verified alternatives chahiye.

prompt: The switch policy has a valid standby, but one port group does not fail over. Which setting should be checked?
options: That group’s override, active/standby list and effective policy
Only the unrelated reverse DNS zone
Only the VM’s optical-drive ISO
Only the order of browser tabs
en: A port-group override can change the policy seen at the switch level.
ru: Port-group override switch level par nazar aane wali policy ko badal sakti hai.

prompt: An upstream outage stops traffic while both NIC links remain Up under Link status only. What explains a missed failover?
options: The fault may not change the local link state being monitored
Link status only verifies every remote application
The DNS suffix must have been erased
The failover policy automatically deletes all Standby links
en: Link-state detection has a scope; not every upstream failure produces a local link-down.
ru: Link-state detection ka scope hai; har upstream failure local link-down nahin banata.

prompt: IP-hash teaming is chosen on a standard switch without a compatible upstream aggregation design. What is the concern?
options: The host and physical-switch configuration can be inconsistent and disrupt traffic
IP hash is simply sequential first-IP/second-IP failover
Any two unrelated outer networks are automatically aggregated
IP hash guarantees no upstream configuration is required
en: Standard-switch IP-hash designs require coordinated compatible static aggregation; it is not simple sequential failover.
ru: Standard-switch IP-hash ko coordinated compatible static aggregation chahiye; simple sequential failover nahin.

prompt: A colleague wants to enable LACP directly on a vSphere Standard Switch. What is accurate?
options: LACP is not supported on a standard switch; it requires a suitable distributed-switch design
Every standard switch enables LACP by default
Selecting Explicit failover order enables LACP
Setting a port group to VLAN 0 creates a LAG
en: Do not confuse static aggregation with distributed-switch LACP support.
ru: Static aggregation aur distributed-switch LACP support ko mix na karein.

prompt: Management disconnects during an uplink test. What recovery approach is most appropriate?
options: Use the local console to identify the affected path and restore the recorded management configuration
Reset every network object before identifying the change
Delete all guest disks to force reconnection
Rename the host as the only recovery action
en: Preserved console access and a known rollback avoid unnecessary broad changes.
ru: Console access aur known rollback unnecessary broad changes se bachate hain.
